rationale: F17 (2026-10-31): the value of a `name:` option is not always a string literal — it can be an IMPORTED IDENTIFIER, whose value lives in another module. The analyzer took the value node's text whatever its type, so the component's identity became the VARIABLE's name: option.vue published `COMPONENT_NAME` with 21 edges sourced at it, select.vue with 43. A name that is not written anywhere as this component's name is a graph lie, and a worse one than the stem fallback F8 chose deliberately, so a non-literal `name:` now keeps the stem AND records `declaredNameUnreadable`. The forbid rows are the point of this fixture: `COMPONENT_NAME` must not be published under either spelling, and `component-name-identifier` (the file stem) must be — which is what F8's fallback already did correctly for a component that declares no name at all, so the two cases are now indistinguishable in the name and distinguishable in the metadata.
